question: Which of the following body areas has the highest density of sebaceous glands?
explanation: Sebaceous glands are most heavily concentrated on the face, chest, and back, which is why those areas produce the most oil. [learn more](BMP111_U4_T10#BMP111_U4_T10_h1)

question: What structure are sebaceous glands typically attached to in the skin?
explanation: Most sebaceous glands connect directly to hair follicles to discharge their oily secretions onto the hair shaft and skin surface. [learn more](BMP111_U4_T10#BMP111_U4_T10_h1)

question: How do sebaceous glands release their oily product?

options.A: By pushing tiny droplets through the cell wall
options.B: By pumping fluid out using active transport
options.C: By bursting open and destroying the whole cell
options.D: By leaking slowly through open pores without cell loss

explanation: Holocrine secretion means the glandular cells fill up with oil and completely disintegrate to release their contents. [learn more](BMP111_U4_T10#BMP111_U4_T10_h2)

question: Why must sebaceous glands continuously produce new cells in their basal layer?

options.A: To prevent the hair follicle from becoming blocked by sweat
options.B: To cool down the skin surface during heavy physical exercise
options.C: To replace cells that are completely destroyed during secretion
options.D: To help the skin absorb moisture from the surrounding air

explanation: Since holocrine cells die and break apart to release sebum, the gland relies on continuous cell division to keep functioning. [learn more](BMP111_U4_T10#BMP111_U4_T10_h2)

question: What is the primary substance that makes up sebum?
explanation: Sebum is an oily substance composed mainly of various lipids like triglycerides, wax esters, and squalene. [learn more](BMP111_U4_T10#BMP111_U4_T10_h3)

question: How does sebum help protect the skin from infection?

options.A: By washing away dust particles through continuous liquid flow
options.B: By creating an acidic oily layer that stops harmful bacteria from growing
options.C: By sending white blood cells directly to the outer layer of the skin
options.D: By freezing surface pathogens when environmental temperatures drop

explanation: The lipid composition and mild acidity of sebum create an unfavorable environment for many harmful microorganisms. [learn more](BMP111_U4_T10#BMP111_U4_T10_h3)

question: Which group of hormones is primarily responsible for stimulating sebaceous glands?
explanation: Androgens are the main hormones that trigger sebaceous gland growth and oil production, especially starting around puberty. [learn more](BMP111_U4_T10#BMP111_U4_T10_h4)

question: Why do children typically experience a decrease in skin oiliness compared to teenagers?

options.A: Because sweat glands block sebum production in young children
options.B: Because children consume less fat in their daily diet
options.C: Because the skin sheds its outer layer much faster in youth
options.D: Because androgen hormone levels are very low during childhood

explanation: Sebaceous glands remain relatively inactive through childhood until rising pubertal androgens reactivate them. [learn more](BMP111_U4_T10#BMP111_U4_T10_h4)

question: Which of the following conditions involves blocked sebaceous ducts leading to trapped oil under the skin?
explanation: A sebaceous cyst forms when a gland or its duct gets blocked, allowing sebum to build up into a smooth lump under the skin. [learn more](BMP111_U4_T10#BMP111_U4_T10_h5)

question: What is NOT a key factor in the development of acne vulgaris?

options.D: Low water intake causing dry skin

explanation: Acne is driven by hormones, excess oil, dead skin buildup, and bacteria—not by drinking too little water. [learn more](BMP111_U4_T10#BMP111_U4_T10_h5)
